summary:
Four referred items, all four re-verified against the CURRENT tree before any edit and all four reproduced -- none was already fixed, none was wrong. THREE CLOSED ON BOTH SIDES AT ONCE, which is why they were referred: ITEM 1 (two frozen EVAL signatures with no channel for outputs they declare) is closed by widening, ITEM 2 (the refusal for an armed-but-dishonest vocabulary lift) is closed by a new entry in observe's closed block-reason set, ITEM 3 (four stale claims that compose() stops at RUN.process_setup) is corrected in all four places. ITEM 4 is a REFUTED defect: .rework/ISSUES.md P2-H11's ruling still holds, eval's eight P5/P6 markers stay, and the re-check is now written into src/eval/api.py::<module> so the next agent does not 'fix' it.

WHERE compose() ACTUALLY STOPS, measured by running the document's own command: `NotImplementedError: CAP.startup_refusals: P4 (capacity) fills this in` -- the 29th of the 39 rows in spine/compose.py::ASSEMBLY_ORDER, PAST CAP.new_valve. RUN.process_setup is the FIRST row and has had a body since D12. So the stale claim was not slightly stale: the root now reaches past the resume, the corpus, the vocabulary, the model, the fabric, the store, the partition and the valve, and the valve's two Gates are readable on every compose() without writing a line. K13 could not see any of the four copies because what rots there is a symbol name and K13 reads digits.

NO WIRE WAS SPENT AND NONE WAS NEEDED. Re-counted today: tests/test_couplings.py prints '23 coupling(s) resolved ...; 19 wire(s) of 25 budgeted, 4 intra-package', so SIX edges remain, and the 'two left' src/eval/api.py carried until today was the couplings-as-wires conflation. For curve_probe's `step` a wire was never even available -- a Coupling.compute receives only frozen Configs and a window counter is runtime state, the same ground spine/assemble.py::NOT_WIRES already refuses d_curve_bpb and d_shift_at on. For verification_fit's `verify_mode` a wire WAS mechanically available and lost on its merits, not its price.

SUITE: 5 of 6 files fully green. ONE CHECK IS RED AND IT IS MINE, BY DESIGN AND WITH THE FIX PROVEN: K12 reads `verify_mode` as an argument with no producer because it computes 'produced' from the order tables' row prose and a DEFERRED entry point has no row. The one-clause repair belongs in src/spine/compose.py, which I do not own. I applied it in a scratch copy outside the repository and the contract suite goes to '14 checks + 46 self-test cases, 0 failing'. The exact find/replace is under unfinished, and the residue is recorded in the tree as well as here -- in docs/04_CONTRACT.md's deferral table row and in Q-EVAL-11 -- so it is not lost if this report is.

recommendation.chose:
ITEM 1: WIDEN BOTH SIGNATURES, and pass both values as ARGUMENTS the composition root supplies. curve_probe(ev, *, units_by_domain, logits_fn, step, rng) and verification_fit(ev, *, store_copy, verify_mode, rng), moved in docs/04_CONTRACT.md's ```contract block and in src/eval/api.py in the same edit so K1 stays green in both directions. Recorded as docs/04_CONTRACT.md::Q-EVAL-11 with the alternatives, the costs and the falsifier.

ITEM 2: ADD `dead_rows_unmasked` TO Decision.block_reason's CLOSED SET rather than a third CAP.startup_refusals clause. It bites on the VOCABULARY arm only, it is EVALUATED LAST (after at_hard_ceiling), and the flag it reads is frozen onto the Valve at new_valve as counters['cap.mask_dead_rows'] so CAP.observe's 'WIRES READ: none' stays true.
recommendation.alternatives:
ITEM 1, gap A (`step`). (A) Argument -- taken. (B) A wire: NOT AVAILABLE. spine/wire.py's Coupling.compute receives only frozen Configs and Config freezes when build() returns; `step` is RUN's per-window counter. docs/04_CONTRACT.md's own refused-candidates table already refuses d_curve_bpb and d_shift_at on exactly that ground. So the space is one option wide and this report says so rather than inventing a loser. (C) Let EVAL keep its own counter: refused -- a second source of truth for RUN.RunClock, which is the C12 shape.

ITEM 1, gap B (`verify_mode`). (A) Argument -- taken. COST: K12 residue in a file I do not own (below), and the value is invisible to affects() until a row spells it. (B) A WIRE, EVAL.d_verify_mode <- MEM.verify. It is mechanically legal -- MEM.verify is a frozen NAME lever -- and it lost on three counts, none of them the budget: (i) EVAL DECLARES NO WIRES AND RECEIVES NONE, which src/eval/api.py, src/eval/levers.py and docs/04_CONTRACT.md all state, and that is a design statement ('everything that measures the run and nothing that changes it') rather than an accident -- a value consumed to RENDER A GATE never reaches a mechanism; (ii) the tree's live idiom for a frozen lever crossing a boundary into a constructor is a root-passed argument, and spine/compose.py already ships three of them -- MEM.open_store(vocab_slots=LM.vocab_slots, lm_kind=LM.arch) and DOM.open_partition(sig_dim=SIG.d); (iii) it needs TWO files I do not own (a Coupling row in src/spine/assemble.py and the 'no wires' prose in src/eval/levers.py) against the argument's ONE, so it is the larger residue as well as the larger commitment. (C) Recover the mode from `store_copy`: refused, and re-checked today -- memory/api.py::Store.__slots__ has no verify field, and inferring it from whether Store.recon or Store.selfcon holds values reads a CONFIGURATION OFF THE DATA. (D) Mint an EVAL_VERIFY_MODE lever: refused -- a second declaration of MEM.verify, and MEM_VERIFY=off with EVAL_VERIFY_MODE=selfcon prints a Gate that lies, which is the L1 shape the spine exists to remove. (E) Delete the Gate or the field: the compromise this task forbids, and the one the previous two passes also refused.

ITEM 2. (A) A block_reason in observe's closed set -- taken. COST: at CAP_TARGETS in (vocab, both) with the shipped LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=False the vocabulary arm now declines lifts it used to take; the word FIRED on cap.vocab_arm_honest is unchanged and the histogram carries the cost. (B) A THIRD CAP.startup_refusals CLAUSE. COST, and it is why it lost: it makes a configuration that runs today unrunnable -- LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS defaults to False (src/lm/levers.py::LMLevers.mask_dead_rows), so CAP_TARGETS=vocab would die at startup on the shipped defaults -- and spine/assemble.py's CAP.d_mask_dead_rows row names that stricter repair as THE OWNER'S TO ASK FOR in as many words: 'a valve that refused to lift the vocabulary at all while the mask is off would need no flag, and that is the stricter repair if the owner wants it.' Taking an owner's call is not mine to take. (C) Leave it: the status quo the previous pass chose deliberately. COST: the package keeps a mechanism whose own printed reason says nothing in the tree refuses it, which is the sentence this item exists to retire. (D) Both (A) and (B): redundant, and it still takes the owner's call.

ITEM 2, THE ORDER WITHIN (A), which is the sub-decision that actually matters. Placed FIRST -- beside targets_off, which it resembles in being knowable at startup -- `dead_rows_unmasked` would answer EVERY call on an unmasked run and the histogram would never learn whether the vocabulary arm ever pinned and stalled. That is precisely the '0 lifts alone cannot distinguish never full from never plateaued' collapse the closed set was written to end, rebuilt one entry later. Placed LAST it counts exactly the lifts that were EARNED AND THEN DECLINED for dishonesty, a number no other line in the run carries.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER, per item.
ITEM 1 gap A: if RUN ever hands instruments a RunClock RECORD rather than a bare index, `step` should ride on that record instead of as a scalar -- one object, not one argument per field. Re-open then, not before.
ITEM 1 gap B: if a SECOND EVAL entry point turns out to need MEM.verify, the argument stops being cheaper than the wire. Two call sites passing one frozen lever is exactly the shape the nine promotions in docs/04_CONTRACT.md section 0 were made from, and EVAL.d_verify_mode should then be declared against the six remaining edges. The measurement is a grep of the P6 rows when they land: more than one consumer means wire it.
ITEM 2: the falsifier is a run, and it is cheap. Build CAP at CAP_TARGETS=vocab, CAP_VOCAB_START well below the ceiling, LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=0, and let P4's observe run to a lift: if CAP.counters' block-reason histogram shows `dead_rows_unmasked` accumulating while not_pinned / not_stalled / threshold ALSO show nonzero counts, the last-place ordering is doing its job. If `dead_rows_unmasked` is the only nonzero key, it was placed too early after all and the ordering argument is wrong. That distinction is unobservable today because CAP.observe is a stub, which is stated rather than hidden.
ITEM 2, THE OWNER'S OPEN CALL, unchanged by this edit: whether to take the STRICTER repair -- a valve that refuses the vocabulary arm outright while the mask is off, which spine/assemble.py::COUPLINGS' CAP.d_mask_dead_rows row records as the owner's to ask for and which would make that wire reducible. This edit deliberately does not take it.
